q: A pavement and a footpath are both available. Where should a pedestrian walk?
exp: The pavement or footpath is the first choice for pedestrians. Bicycle paths are the next option only when neither is available.

q: The driver ahead has moved left and signalled a left turn. On which side should you pass, when it is safe?
exp: A driver positioned to the left and signalling a left turn is passed on the right. This is an exception to the usual left-side overtaking rule.

q: Your light is green, but a queue prevents you from clearing the intersection. What should you do?
opts: Enter and wait in the middle
Wait before the intersection until you can clear it
exp: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely. A green light does not justify blocking it.

q: Two cars approach an equivalent, unregulated intersection on paved roads. The other car comes from your right. Who must give way?
opts: The other driver must give way
The slower car must give way
exp: At an equivalent intersection without signs, lights or another applicable exception, drivers give way to drivers approaching from the right.

q: You are turning left. An oncoming car on the same road is turning right into the same road as you. No signs or lights change the ordinary rule. What must you do?
opts: Go first because your turn is longer
Give way to the oncoming car
Go first if you indicated earlier
Ask the other driver to reverse
exp: A driver turning left must give way to an oncoming driver turning right at the same intersection.

q: You are below the posted speed limit, but cannot stop within the clear distance you can see. What does the chapter say?
opts: Your speed is acceptable because it is below the limit
Only trucks need to slow down
You are still driving too fast and must slow down
Using high-beam headlights removes the need to slow down
exp: You must be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead and that is clear. Staying below a posted limit alone is not enough.

q: What does a broken yellow line alongside the road prohibit?
opts: Every brief stop to let a passenger out
exp: A broken yellow line prohibits parking. A solid yellow line prohibits stopping. Other restrictions can also apply at the location.

q: There is heavy rain but no fog or snowfall. May you use the rear fog light just because of the rain?
exp: Rear fog lights may be used when fog or snowfall reduces visibility to less than 50 metres, not merely because of heavy rain.

q: An electronic sign shows a red cross above a rush-hour lane. What does it mean?
opts: Use the lane only for overtaking
The lane is closed; do not drive on it
The lane is open to cars only
The lane has a lower speed limit
exp: A rush-hour lane may be used when officially open. A red cross means that the lane is closed.

q: What is the maximum speed inside an erf?
opts: Walking speed with no numerical limit
exp: The chapter states a statutory maximum of 15 km/h inside an erf. Drivers must also adapt to pedestrians sharing the space.

q: What determines priority at a roundabout?
opts: The signs and road markings, or ordinary priority rules if none regulate it
Traffic already on the roundabout always has priority
The largest vehicle always has priority
exp: Check the signs and shark's teeth. If no priority signs or markings regulate the roundabout, the ordinary rule of giving way to drivers from the right applies.

q: What is the maximum distance between the rear of a towing motor vehicle and the front of the motor vehicle being towed?
exp: The distance between the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle may be no more than 5 metres. The arrangement must also be safe and controllable.

q: You are pulling out of a parking space as a pedestrian and a cyclist approach your path. Who must you give way to?
opts: Both the pedestrian and the cyclist
Only vehicles approaching from the right
exp: Moving from a parking space is a special manoeuvre. You must first give way to all other traffic, including pedestrians and cyclists.

q: You want to fit a rear-facing child seat on a front passenger seat equipped with a front airbag. What is required?
opts: Use only the adult seatbelt instead
exp: A rear-facing child seat may be used on a seat with a front airbag only if that airbag has been deactivated.

q: A cyclist holds a phone to check navigation while riding. Is this permitted?
opts: No, the handheld-device prohibition also applies to cyclists
Yes, if no call is being made
exp: The prohibition on holding a mobile electronic device while driving also applies to cyclists, including when checking navigation. Stop safely before using the phone by hand.

q: Unless another rule provides otherwise, what is the basic road-position rule for drivers?
opts: Keep as far right as possible
Choose any lane regardless of traffic
exp: The chapter gives keeping as far to the right as possible as the fundamental position rule.

q: A mandatory bicycle path is present. Where must a cyclist on an ordinary bicycle ride?
exp: Cyclists must use a mandatory bicycle path or combined bicycle/moped path where one is present. The chapter separately describes exceptions for wide bicycles.

q: You approach a zebra crossing behind a slow vehicle. May you overtake immediately before or on the crossing?
opts: Yes, if no pedestrian is visible
exp: Overtaking a vehicle immediately before or on a pedestrian crossing is prohibited.

q: Traffic is moving slowly in queues in lanes going in the same direction. May the queue on the right pass the queue on the left?
opts: Only if the left lane is empty
exp: When traffic is moving in queues, passing a queue on the right is an exception to the normal overtaking rule.

q: You approach from an unpaved road. A car on a paved road approaches from your left. With no signs or lights changing the rule, who gives way?
opts: You give way to the car on the paved road
The car on the paved road gives way
Only a turning driver gives way
exp: Drivers on an unpaved road give way to drivers on a paved road, regardless of which side they approach from.

q: At an otherwise unregulated intersection, a tram approaches your car from the left. What is the ordinary priority rule?
opts: Your car has priority because it comes from the right
You give way to the tram
Trams have priority only at night
exp: At an otherwise unregulated intersection, drivers give way to trams. Lights, signs or authorised instructions may determine a different order.

q: The railway crossing is open, but the queue beyond it leaves no room for your whole vehicle. What should you do?
opts: Enter if no train is visible
Stop on the tracks until the queue moves
Wait before the crossing until you can clear it completely
Follow the car ahead without leaving a gap
exp: You may enter a level crossing only when you can pass through immediately and clear it completely.

q: When should you signal an intended turn?
opts: Only after entering the new road
Only when another vehicle is behind you
exp: Signal before turning, using the indicator or an arm signal if no indicator is fitted.

q: What does a solid yellow line alongside the road prohibit?
opts: Only parking for more than five minutes
exp: A solid yellow line prohibits stopping, unlike a broken yellow line which prohibits parking.

q: According to the chapter, which brief stop is an exception to the bus-stop stopping restriction?
opts: Waiting for someone who is still at home
Immediately letting a passenger board or get out
Leaving the car to buy a ticket
exp: The bus-stop restriction has an exception for immediately boarding or alighting passengers. It does not allow parking there.

q: How close to an intersection is parking prohibited?
exp: The chapter prohibits parking within 5 metres of an intersection.

q: A blue-zone sign requires a parking disc. What must you display?
opts: A note with your telephone number
The time you intend to leave
A clearly visible parking disc showing arrival time
exp: Where time-limited parking requires a parking disc, display the arrival time clearly through the windscreen and respect the permitted duration.

q: How should a parked bicycle or moped be positioned?
opts: So other road users can pass freely
Across the footpath to make it visible
Where it blocks the least expensive vehicle
exp: Bicycles and mopeds must not be placed in a way that obstructs pedestrians, cyclists or other road users.

q: Which situation justifies using the horn?
exp: Sound and flashing-light signals are used to avert imminent danger, not merely as greetings or expressions of frustration.

q: Which front lights must a motor vehicle use while driving at night?
opts: Fog lights only, in all weather
exp: Motor vehicles must use dipped headlights at night and in reduced visibility.

q: Which front and rear light combination does the chapter require for a bicycle ridden at night?
opts: Flashing red at the front and white at the rear
A red light at both ends
A steady white or yellow front light and a steady red rear light
exp: The bicycle lighting list specifies a non-flashing white or yellow front light and a non-flashing red rear light, as well as the required reflectors.

q: A road-work vehicle uses an amber flashing light. Does that light give it priority?
opts: No, it warns of a special or dangerous situation
Yes, if it is moving slowly
exp: An amber or yellow rotating or flashing light warns other road users. It does not give the vehicle priority.

q: Your motor vehicle is stationary at night on the carriageway outside a built-up area. Which lights does the chapter require?
opts: No lights if the engine is off
The prescribed front and rear parking/position lights
exp: A motor vehicle stationary at night on the carriageway outside a built-up area must show the prescribed front and rear parking/position lights.

q: What does a green flashing light identify during authorised emergency-service operations?
opts: A vehicle exempt from speed limits
exp: A green flashing light identifies a command function. It does not by itself create priority.

q: What minimum construction-related speed capability and permission does the chapter specify for motorway access?
exp: Vehicles that cannot or may not travel at least 60 km/h are excluded from motorways. Other vehicle-category restrictions also apply; this is not a minimum driving speed in every situation.

q: For an autoweg, what speed must a motor vehicle, by construction, be able and permitted to reach?
exp: An autoweg is intended for motor vehicles that can and may travel at least 50 km/h by construction. This is an access condition, not a requirement to maintain that speed in all conditions.

q: You miss your motorway exit. May you reverse along the motorway to reach it?
opts: No, reversing on a motorway is prohibited
Yes, if the exit is less than 50 metres away
exp: Reversing and turning around are prohibited on motorways.

q: Where may you park inside an erf?
opts: Anywhere if pedestrians can squeeze past
Only in designated marked parking spaces
Anywhere for less than an hour
exp: Parking inside an erf is permitted only in designated marked parking spaces.

q: When leaving a roundabout, what signal should you give?
exp: Signal right before leaving the roundabout so waiting drivers know you are exiting.

q: A pedestrian is clearly about to step onto a zebra crossing. What should a driver do?
opts: Continue until the pedestrian reaches the middle
Give way only after the pedestrian waves
exp: Drivers give way to pedestrians on a crossing or clearly about to step onto it.

q: An ambulance responding to an emergency approaches with a blue flashing light and siren. What should you do?
opts: Accelerate to stay ahead of it
Make way as quickly as safely possible, stopping if necessary
Always drive through a red light to clear its path
Stop immediately wherever you are, even if that blocks it
exp: Give way safely and avoid blocking the priority vehicle. Making way does not allow you to ignore traffic lights or endanger others.

q: You encounter loose animals near the road. What is the appropriate response?
opts: Slow down and pass with as much space as possible
Keep your speed because animals must yield
exp: Animals are unpredictable. Slow down, take precautions and give them space; a horn can startle them.

q: When a warning triangle is used for an obstructing stationary vehicle, approximately where should it be placed?
opts: 30 metres from the vehicle toward approaching traffic
exp: Place the triangle about 30 metres from the vehicle in the direction from which traffic approaches.

q: An obstructing stationary vehicle has working hazard warning lights switched on. Does the chapter also require a warning triangle?
opts: No, a triangle is not required when the hazard lights are operating
exp: Approaching drivers must be warned about an obstacle they may not notice in time. Operating hazard lights mean a triangle is not required.

q: In an ordinary passenger car, may a passenger travel in the boot instead of a designated seat?
opts: Yes, if all seats are occupied
exp: Passengers must use designated seats. The boot is not a passenger seat.

q: How should a seatbelt be worn?
opts: With the shoulder belt under the arm
Loose enough to move freely out of the seat
Correctly across the shoulder and chest
Only across the lap even when a shoulder belt is fitted
exp: The chapter says the belt must be worn correctly across the shoulder and chest, not tucked under the arm.

q: Below what height must a child generally use an approved child restraint suitable for them?
exp: Children under 1.35 metres generally need an approved, suitable child restraint fitted correctly.

q: Does the helmet requirement also apply to snorfiets riders and their passengers?
opts: Yes, they must wear an approved helmet
No, because a snorfiets is slower
exp: Snorfiets riders and passengers must also wear an approved helmet. The chapter allows an approved moped or speed-pedelec helmet for a snorfiets rider.

q: What seating support is required for a child under 8 carried on a bicycle?
opts: Sufficient support for the back, hands and feet
No support if the child can hold the rider
Only a cushion on the luggage rack
exp: A child under 8 needs a safe seating position supporting the back, hands and feet, such as a suitable child seat.

q: Which statement about using a securely mounted phone is consistent with the chapter?
opts: A mount permits all distracting use
Use without holding it is permitted in principle, provided it causes no danger or obstruction
A mounted phone may be held whenever the road is straight
exp: Hands-free use is permitted in principle when the device is not held and its use does not endanger or hinder traffic. Attention to traffic remains essential.
